ai.literal: Among things obtained, that which we know is not; other than the blessing of children who have known knowledge, other things.
ai.translation: Among all the things one can acquire, we know of no greater blessing than having children who possess wisdom.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் பெறும் செல்வங்கள் எல்லாவற்றுள்ளும், அறிவுடைய பிள்ளைகளைப் பெறும் பேற்றினைத் தவிர வேறு சிறந்த பேறு இருப்பதாக நாம் அறியவில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet evaluates the greatest possible acquisition in human life. The phrase 'பெறும் அவற்றுள்' (among things obtained) sets up a comparison of all forms of wealth, status, or possessions. The poet emphatically states 'யாம் அறிவது இல்லை' (we know of nothing) to dismiss all other achievements. The true treasure is defined as 'அறிவு அறிந்த மக்கட்பேறு' (the blessing of children who possess knowledge). Here, the repetition of the root for knowledge emphasizes not just having offspring, but raising children who have actively cultivated wisdom and good character.

ai.literal: Seven births-in evil-things touch-not blame appear-not character possessing children obtain-if.
ai.translation: If one begets children of blameless character, evil will not touch them throughout all seven births.
ai.modern: பழி இல்லாத நல்ல பண்புகளை உடைய பிள்ளைகளைப் பெற்றால், ஒருவரை ஏழு பிறவிகளிலும் எந்தத் தீமையும் தீண்டாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the lasting value of raising children with good character. The phrase 'pali piranga' means blame or fault does not appear, highlighting a spotless reputation. If parents raise such virtuous children, the text states that 'evil things will not touch' them across 'seven births', a traditional idiom for an immeasurable span of time. The merit of having good children protects the parents from suffering indefinitely.

ai.literal: One's own wealth, they say, one's own children; their wealth by their respective deeds will come.
ai.translation: It is said that one's own children are one's true wealth, and that this wealth comes to a person through their own respective deeds.
ai.modern: தம் மக்கள் தான் தம்முடைய உண்மையான செல்வம் என்று கூறுவர்; அந்தச் செல்வமானது அவரவர் செய்யும் செயல்களின் வழியாகவே வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines children as the true wealth of a person. The phrase 'they say' indicates an accepted wisdom that material wealth is secondary to one's offspring. The word 'அவர்' (their) in the second line refers to the children, making 'அவர் பொருள்' mean 'the wealth that is them'. The second half explains that this precious wealth is attained as a result of the parents' own respective deeds. Thus, the blessing of having good children is directly linked to one's own actions.

ai.literal: Even than ambrosia, exceedingly sweet indeed is one's own children's small hands mixed porridge.
ai.translation: The simple porridge stirred by the tiny hands of one's own children is far sweeter than the nectar of the gods.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய குழந்தைகளின் சிறிய கைகளால் பிசையப்பட்ட உணவு, அமிழ்தத்தை விட மிகவும் இனிமையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the pure joy of parenthood through a simple, everyday image. It states that ordinary food becomes sweeter than the mythical nectar of the gods when it has been playfully mixed by the tiny hands of one's own children. The word 'அமிழ்து' represents the ultimate delicacy, yet it is surpassed by the emotional sweetness of a child's touch. The imagery of 'சிறுகை அளாவிய கூழ்' evokes the messy, endearing reality of feeding toddlers, highlighting how parental love transforms the mundane into the extraordinary.

ai.literal: Children's body touching is joy to the body; moreover their word hearing is joy to the ear.
ai.translation: The touch of one's children brings joy to the body, and hearing their words brings joy to the ear.
ai.modern: தம் குழந்தைகளின் உடலைத் தழுவுவது உடலுக்கு இன்பம் தரும்; அவர்களின் மழலைச் சொற்களைக் கேட்பது காதுக்கு இன்பம் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the physical and emotional joys of parenthood. It states that embracing one's children provides the greatest tactile pleasure for the body. Similarly, listening to their innocent words offers the sweetest music to the ears, highlighting how children delight the senses of their parents.

ai.literal: Flute is sweet, lute is sweet, they say - their own children's prattling words those who have not heard.
ai.translation: Only those who have not heard the prattling words of their own children will say that the flute and the lute are sweet.
ai.modern: தங்கள் குழந்தைகளின் மழலைச் சொற்களைக் கேட்காதவர்கள் மட்டுமே குழலின் இசையும் யாழின் இசையும் இனிமையானவை என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the beauty of instrumental music with the sound of a child's voice. It states that people praise the sweetness of the flute and the lute only until they hear their own children babble. The words 'குழல்' (flute) and 'யாழ்' (lute) represent the highest forms of refined music. Yet, the natural, unpolished 'மழலை' (prattle) of one's own children surpasses them in sweetness, highlighting the unparalleled joy of parenthood.

ai.literal: Father to son doing good deed, in assembly being first to sit making.
ai.translation: The greatest good a father can do for his son is to make him worthy of sitting at the forefront of the assembly.
ai.modern: ஒரு தந்தை தன் மகனுக்குச் செய்யும் நன்மை, அவனை அறிஞர்கள் அவையில் முன்னணியில் இருக்கும்படி தகுதியுடையவனாக ஆக்குவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the primary duty of a father towards his child. The phrase 'அவையத்து முந்தி இருப்பச் செயல்' (making him sit first in the assembly) means equipping the son with enough knowledge and character to be respected among the wise. The word 'நன்றி' (good deed or benefit) highlights that this is the most valuable gift a parent can provide. Rather than merely leaving behind wealth, a father's true contribution is raising a child capable of leading and excelling in society.

ai.literal: Than themselves, their children's possession of wisdom, on the great earth, to enduring living beings all, is sweet.
ai.translation: That their children possess wisdom greater than their own is a joy to all living beings on this great earth.
ai.modern: தம்மை விடத் தம் பிள்ளைகள் அறிவுடையவர்களாக இருப்பது, இந்தப் பெரிய உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் மகிழ்ச்சி தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet expresses the universal joy of seeing the next generation surpass the current one. The word 'tammin' means 'than themselves', setting up a comparison between the parents and their children. 'Arivudaimai' denotes the possession of wisdom. The poet states that on this great earth, it is a sweet and natural joy for all living beings to see their offspring possess greater wisdom than they do. This highlights that the desire for one's children to excel is a fundamental trait of all life.

ai.literal: who bore than the time greatly will rejoice her own son noble man that who heard mother
ai.translation: A mother who hears her son praised as a noble man will rejoice even more than at the time she bore him.
ai.modern: தன் மகனைச் சான்றோன் என்று பிறர் சொல்லக் கேட்ட தாய், அவனைப் பெற்றெடுத்த காலத்தில் அடைந்த மகிழ்ச்சியை விடப் பெரும் மகிழ்ச்சி அடைவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate joy of a mother. The word 'பொழுதின்' uses the suffix 'இன்' to mean 'more than the time', comparing two moments of immense happiness. When she hears others praise her son as 'சான்றோன்' (a noble or perfect man), her joy surpasses even the profound happiness she felt at his birth. It emphasizes that a child's virtuous character is the greatest reward for a parent.

ai.literal: Son to father rendering help: 'this man's father what penance did he perform, I wonder' saying word.
ai.translation: The greatest help a son can render his father is to live so well that the world asks, 'What penance did his father perform to beget him?'
ai.modern: ஒரு மகன் தன் தந்தைக்குச் செய்யும் கைம்மாறு, இவனுடைய தந்தை இவனைப் பிள்ளையாகப் பெற என்ன தவம் செய்தானோ என்று உலகத்தார் வியந்து கூறும் சொல்லைப் பெற்றுத் தருவதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate gratitude a son can show his father. The word 'உதவி' (help) here means the reciprocal duty or return a son owes. The greatest return is not material wealth, but living such an exemplary life that onlookers marvel at it. They will wonder aloud, 'என் நோற்றான் கொல்' (what penance did he perform?), implying the father must have done great austerities to be blessed with such a son. Thus, earning this specific word of praise from the world is the highest tribute a son can pay.
